    Bitstring encodings

    ClassBitstring encodings#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.BitstringEncoding

    A canonical bitstring encoding of a type \(\alpha\) consists of an encoding map from \(\alpha\) to finite lists of booleans and a partial decoding map from finite lists of booleans to \(\alpha\), such that decoding the encoding of any \(a \in \alpha\) succeeds and returns \(a\).

    class BitstringEncoding α extends Computability.Encoding α Bool

    • a class version of Mathlib's Computability.Encoding specialized to the alphabet Bool, inlined from FormalConjectures (absent from Mathlib).

    Bitstring Encoding

    DefinitionEncoding function of a bitstring encoding#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.BitstringEncoding.bitEncode

    For a type \(\alpha\) with a canonical bitstring encoding, the bitstring encoding of \(a \in \alpha\) is the finite list of booleans that this encoding assigns to \(a\).

    def bitEncode [BitstringEncoding α] (a : α) : List Bool := toEncoding.encode a
    class BitstringEncoding α extends Computability.Encoding α Bool

    MetaMathlibExt.BitstringEncoding.bitDecode

    For a type \(\alpha\) with a canonical bitstring encoding, bitstring decoding is the decoding function of that encoding: it sends each finite list of booleans either to an element of \(\alpha\) or to failure.

    def bitDecode [BitstringEncoding α] (l : List Bool) : Option α := toEncoding.decode l
    class BitstringEncoding α extends Computability.Encoding α Bool

    TheoremDecoding inverts bitstring encoding#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.BitstringEncoding.bitDecode_bitEncode

    Let \(\alpha\) be a type with a canonical bitstring encoding. For every \(a \in \alpha\), decoding the bitstring encoding of \(a\) succeeds and returns \(a\).

    @[simp]
theorem bitDecode_bitEncode [BitstringEncoding α] (a : α) :
    bitDecode (bitEncode a) = some a
    class BitstringEncoding α extends Computability.Encoding α Bool

    DefinitionSelf-delimiting form of a bitstring#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.BitstringEncoding.delimit

    The self-delimiting form of a bitstring \((b_1, \dots, b_n)\) is \((\mathrm{true}, b_1, \dots, \mathrm{true}, b_n, \mathrm{false})\): each bit is preceded by \(\mathrm{true}\) and the block is terminated by \(\mathrm{false}\). In particular the empty bitstring becomes \((\mathrm{false})\).

    def delimit : List Bool → List Bool
  | [] => [false]
  | b :: l => true :: b :: delimit l

    MetaMathlibExt.BitstringEncoding.undelimit

    Write booleans as bits, with true as \(1\) and false as \(0\). Reading a list of bits from the front, a \(0\) ends the block, and a \(1\) followed by a bit \(b\) contributes \(b\) to the payload. The result is the payload together with the rest of the list after the terminating \(0\). Parsing fails if the list runs out before a terminating \(0\) is read.

    def undelimit : List Bool → Option (List Bool × List Bool)
  | false :: rest => some ([], rest)
  | true :: b :: input => (undelimit input).map fun p => (b :: p.1, p.2)
  | _ => none

    DefinitionBounded parsing of self-delimiting blocks#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.BitstringEncoding.undelimitBlocksAux

    Given a bound \(n\) and a list of booleans \(s\), the parse returns the empty list of payloads if \(s\) is empty. If \(s\) is nonempty and \(n = 0\) it fails. If \(s\) is nonempty and \(n = m + 1\), it parses one self-delimiting block from the front of \(s\), then parses the remaining list with bound \(m\), and returns the first payload followed by the payloads of the rest. It fails if either step fails. So the parse succeeds exactly when \(s\) is the concatenation of at most \(n\) self-delimiting blocks, and it returns their payloads in order.

    def undelimitBlocksAux : ℕ → List Bool → Option (List (List Bool))
  | _, [] => some []
  | 0, _ :: _ => none
  | fuel + 1, input =>
    (undelimit input).bind fun p => (undelimitBlocksAux fuel p.2).map (p.1 :: ·)
    def undelimit : List Bool → Option (List Bool × List Bool)
  | false :: rest => some ([], rest)
  | true :: b :: input => (undelimit input).map fun p => (b :: p.1, p.2)
  | _ => none

    DefinitionParsing a list of booleans into self-delimiting blocks#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.BitstringEncoding.undelimitBlocks

    Given a list of booleans \(s\), this repeatedly parses one self-delimiting block from the front of \(s\) until \(s\) is used up, allowing at most as many blocks as the length of \(s\), and returns the list of payloads in order. It fails if some block fails to parse. The bound never binds, since every block uses at least one bit. So the parse succeeds exactly when \(s\) is a concatenation of self-delimiting blocks.

    def undelimitBlocks (input : List Bool) : Option (List (List Bool)) :=
  undelimitBlocksAux input.length input
    def undelimitBlocksAux : ℕ → List Bool → Option (List (List Bool))
  | _, [] => some []
  | 0, _ :: _ => none
  | fuel + 1, input =>
    (undelimit input).bind fun p => (undelimitBlocksAux fuel p.2).map (p.1 :: ·)

    DefinitionPolynomial-time computability under given encodings#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.ComplexityTheory.IsPolyTimeWithEncoding

    Let \(e_\alpha\) encode \(\alpha\) as words over an alphabet \(\Gamma_\alpha\) and \(e_\beta\) encode \(\beta\) as words over \(\Gamma_\beta\). A function \(f : \alpha \to \beta\) is polynomial-time computable with respect to \(e_\alpha\) and \(e_\beta\) when there are a multi-stack Turing machine with finitely many stacks, function labels and internal states and a finite input stack alphabet, identifications of its input and output stack alphabets with \(\Gamma_\alpha\) and \(\Gamma_\beta\), and a polynomial \(p\) with natural-number coefficients, such that for every \(a \in \alpha\) the machine, started at its main function in its initial state with \(e_\alpha(a)\) on its input stack and every other stack empty, halts within \(p(n)\) steps, where \(n\) is the length of \(e_\alpha(a)\), with \(e_\beta(f(a))\) on its output stack, every other stack empty and its internal state equal to its initial state.

    def IsPolyTimeWithEncoding {α β Γα Γβ : Type} (ea : Encoding α Γα)
    (eb : Encoding β Γβ) (f : α → β) :=
  Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime ea.encode eb.encode f)

    Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be types with canonical bitstring encodings. A function \(f : \alpha \to \beta\) is polynomial-time computable when it is polynomial-time computable with respect to the canonical bitstring encodings of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

    def IsPolyTime {α β : Type} [BitstringEncoding α] [BitstringEncoding β]
    (f : α → β) : Prop :=
  IsPolyTimeWithEncoding (BitstringEncoding.toEncoding (α := α))
    (BitstringEncoding.toEncoding (α := β)) f
    class BitstringEncoding α extends Computability.Encoding α Bool

    MathlibExt/Computability/Complexity.lean:48

    def IsPolyTimeWithEncoding {α β Γα Γβ : Type} (ea : Encoding α Γα)
    (eb : Encoding β Γβ) (f : α → β) :=
  Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime ea.encode eb.encode f)

    DefinitionThe complexity class P#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.ComplexityTheory.P

    P is the set of decision problems (functions from lists of booleans to booleans) that are computable in polynomial time by a deterministic multi-stack Turing machine, with respect to the canonical bitstring encodings of inputs and outputs.

    def P : DecisionComplexityClass :=
  { L | IsPolyTime L }
    abbrev DecisionComplexityClass := Set DecisionProblem

    DefinitionThe complexity class NP#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.ComplexityTheory.NP

    NP is the set of decision problems \(L\) (functions from lists of booleans to booleans) for which there exist a polynomial \(p\) with natural-number coefficients and a polynomial-time computable function \(R\) from pairs of lists of booleans to booleans such that, for every list of booleans \(x\), \(L(x)\) is true if and only if there is a list of booleans \(w\) whose length is at most \(p\) evaluated at the length of \(x\) and for which \(R(x, w)\) is true.

    Polynomial time is measured with respect to the canonical bitstring encodings.

    def NP : DecisionComplexityClass :=
  { L | ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ), ∃ R : (List Bool × List Bool) → Bool,
      IsPolyTime R ∧
      ∀ x, L x ↔ ∃ w : List Bool, w.length ≤ p.eval x.length ∧ R (x, w) }
    abbrev DecisionComplexityClass := Set DecisionProblem

    DefinitionThe class coNP#✓fully proved

    MetaMathlibExt.ComplexityTheory.coNP

    The class coNP. coNP is the set of decision problems \(L\) whose complement, the decision problem that accepts exactly the bitstrings that \(L\) rejects, belongs to NP.

    def coNP : DecisionComplexityClass :=
  { L | Lᶜ ∈ NP }
    abbrev DecisionComplexityClass := Set DecisionProblem
